brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Base of four hex pieces (piece:-1,0,0 full; piece:0,0,0 full; piece:1,0,0 full; piece:0,1,0 half-n) locked with three joint bolts; check_build is ok with meshClash clear. Two removable tray bins hold small parts: bin:0,0,0 (full depth, 3 compartments) and bin:-1,0,0 (full depth, 2 compartments).
drawer:0#0,1#cut (style s) sits on the cut face of the half-n base piece:0,1,0.
handle:1,0,0;top sits on cover:1,0,0 (full top cover), with its inserts. The handle is the only carry feature.

The build is one compact cluster about 3 cells across, with a top handle. No weight, battery, or latch was modeled; the configurator does not judge portability beyond size and fit. The drawer and bins are open-topped and not latched, so transport security is not verified.

finish.summary: Built a compact organizer: a four-piece hex base with two removable bins (3-compartment and 2-compartment), one front drawer on a half base, and a carry handle on a top cover. Joint bolts lock the body; the configurator reports no mesh clashes and no errors. Remaining warnings are only informational (open cap faces). Portability beyond the handle and compact size is not verified, and no latch was added for the drawer or bins.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
